pr.title: NEV-1645: Send a practice's report link to its HubSpot contact, behind a marketing flag

decisions.title: Ship the whole send path behind an off-by-default flag that fails closed
decisions.chose: Gate the entire practice-report send behind `marketing-practice-report-send-enabled`, shipped off, with `fallback: false` so an unreachable flag source withholds.
decisions.rejected: Ship the send path live, or use a flag that fails open when LaunchDarkly is unreachable.
decisions.why: With the flag off and no other subscription touched, the PR is a no-op in production until deliberately enabled — so it can land safely and be rolled back by a flag flip during a HubSpot incident, no redeploy. Failing closed means a LaunchDarkly outage withholds sends rather than blasting them.
decisions.quote: Behind a feature flag — `marketing-practice-report-send-enabled` ships **off** in LaunchDarkly and is enabled deliberately after deploy... Fails closed (`fallback: false`); an unreachable flag source withholds.

evidence.claim: The LaunchDarkly evaluation defaults to false and carries only `{ kind: "practice", key: practiceSfAccountId }` in context — no PHI/PII.

decisions.title: Keep the practice-report payload a separate type, not a member of the partner-referral union
decisions.chose: Declare `HubSpotPracticeReportWebhookPayload` as a standalone type and widen `sendHubSpotWebhook` to accept `HubSpotWebhookPayload | HubSpotPracticeReportWebhookPayload`.
decisions.rejected: Add the practice-report shape as another arm of the existing `HubSpotWebhookPayload` union.
decisions.why: The existing union is closed over the partner-referral `EmailType`, and its `buildPartnerReferralWebhookPayload` relies on narrowing that arm. Adding a member with a disjoint `email_type` would break that narrowing and change existing behaviour. A separate type leaves the partner-referral path byte-for-byte untouched.
decisions.quote: Deliberately not a member of HubSpotWebhookPayload: that union is closed over the partner-referral EmailType, and widening it breaks narrowing in buildPartnerReferralWebhookPayload.

evidence.claim: The new payload type is declared separately and `sendHubSpotWebhook` accepts it via a union parameter, rather than extending `HubSpotWebhookPayload`.

* routes to the correct workflow arm.

decisions.title: Order the flow gate → claim → send so a withheld send never claims a slot
decisions.chose: Check the flag first and return early; only then claim the idempotency slot; only then send.
decisions.rejected: Claim the slot up front and then check the flag, or send before recording the claim.
decisions.why: If the flag is off, `practiceReportGenerated` returns before `claim` is ever called, so no slot is consumed — meaning a later flag flip re-drives cleanly instead of finding a phantom claim that suppresses the send. This ordering is what makes the rollback-and-re-enable story work.
decisions.quote: a later flip re-drives cleanly since flag-off never claims a slot.

decisions.title: Make redelivery idempotent via a claim that refuses when the slot is taken
decisions.chose: Claim a slot keyed on `(practice, report_type, batch_period)`; a redelivered event finds the slot claimed, `claim` returns false, and the flow returns before any HubSpot request.
decisions.rejected: POST unconditionally and rely on downstream dedup, or check-then-insert without atomic conflict handling.
decisions.why: Under at-least-once Kafka semantics with `partitionsConsumedConcurrently = 4`, the same event can arrive twice concurrently. `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes the claim atomic, so exactly one delivery wins and the loser makes no HubSpot request and releases nothing it didn't win.
decisions.quote: claim uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (practice_id, report_type, batch_period) DO NOTHING`; redelivery under at-least-once semantics refuses the claim and makes no HubSpot request.

trace.note: logs 'already sent, skipping'; claimSlot returns false.

trace.step: flow returns, no send, no release
trace.note: sendClaimed is never reached; release is not called for a slot not won.

decisions.title: Release the claim on failure via a `sent` flag in `finally`, and rethrow
decisions.chose: Track a `sent` boolean; on any failure (webhook status failed, or thrown error) the `finally` block releases the slot, and the thrown error propagates.
decisions.rejected: Swallow the failure and leave the slot claimed, or release unconditionally including on success.
decisions.why: A failed send that left the slot claimed would permanently suppress retries for that (practice, report_type, batch_period). Releasing only when `sent` is false frees the slot for the next batch while leaving a successful send's claim in place. Rethrowing lets the consumer's retry semantics engage rather than silently dropping the event.
decisions.inferNote: The PR states 'releases the slot on failure' and 'propagates the failure so consumer retry semantics engage' (test names). The `sent`-flag mechanism and the reasoning that only unsuccessful sends release are reconstructed from the code; the release-on-failure intent is stated.

decisions.title: Build a pure-passthrough payload of exactly three fields — no S3, no Couchdrop credential
decisions.chose: `buildPayload` forwards `couchdrop_shared_link_url`, `practice_email`, and `email_type` straight through, with no enrichment reads.
decisions.rejected: Have marketing fetch the report from S3 / Couchdrop or enrich the payload with per-practice data.
decisions.why: Marketing holds no Couchdrop credentials and reads no storage; it simply forwards fields the upstream event already carried. This keeps the blast radius tiny — no new credentials, no storage dependency — and the payload shape is exactly what HubSpot needs (link, recipient, workflow routing).
decisions.quote: Marketing is a **pure passthrough** — it forwards `couchdrop_shared_link_url` + `practice_email` + `email_type` straight through; it reads no S3, calls no Couchdrop, and holds no Couchdrop credentials.

evidence.claim: The composed HubSpot payload is exactly the three forwarded fields, constructed with no storage or credential access.

decisions.title: Adapt the event and rethrow in the Kafka handler; leave the unused `report_type` in the wire schema
decisions.chose: Unwrap `Public<>` values, adapt to a plain message, delegate to the subscription, and rethrow on error; keep `report_type` in the event schema though the handler claims on `email_type`.
decisions.rejected: Swallow handler errors, or strip `report_type` from the schema since the handler doesn't use it.
decisions.why: Rethrowing lets the consumer's at-least-once retry engage instead of silently dropping. `report_type` is the producer's wire contract; removing it would be a schema/contract change and out of scope — a deliberate non-change.
decisions.quote: `PracticeReportEntity.report_type` is declared but unused by the handler (claims key on `email_type`). It is the producer's wire contract; removing it would be a schema/contract change, out of scope.
decisions.note: the retained schema field is a deliberate non-change
